payload.same_tick_producer_consumer_race:
HARD CONFIRMATION, no inference. The 12:00Z tick spawned news-scout-offhours and alert-commander-critical in the same second (12:06:55Z). news-scout produced signal ids 11395-11398 (urgent_news VIC + DBC, chain_catalyst FPT tech sell-off + Brent). alert-commander's committed c256 records its bus read as: "Only bus hit: freshness-sla-monitor urgent_news id11394".

11394 < 11395. The consumer read the bus strictly BEFORE the producer wrote to it, on the same tick, having been spawned in the same second. alert-commander then correctly exited silent -- it had nothing to act on, and its reasoning within the data it could see is sound.

This is the SECOND observation of this exact race in one day: c255's own notebook records the mirror case at 08:0x -- "urgent_news x2 (VIC id11338, VPB id11339 -- both posted ~08:08 by news-scout, AFTER peer c254's earlier bus read)". There, a later sibling caught what the earlier one missed. Here there was no later sibling, so the four signals reached no consumer at all within their window.

This corroborates the already-filed newsscout-4h-cadence-exceeds-2h-signal-ttl-blinds-alertcommander row with a same-tick mechanism the cadence framing does not cover: even at matched cadence, co-spawned producer and consumer race, and the dispatcher fans out in parallel by design (BGFAN-1) so there is no ordering guarantee to lean on. Worth deciding whether alert-commander should re-read the bus late in its cycle, or whether the fanout needs a producer-before-consumer ordering hint for slots that share a tick.
payload.leaf_agent_shared_doc_write_scope:
alert-commander committed b398e4397, a 12-line addition to .claude/skills/commit-mutex/reference.md -- a FLEET-SHARED skill file consumed by every agent that commits.

The content is sound and I am not asking for it to be reverted. It accurately documents a real failure class the skill did not cover: PUSH_EXIT != 0 is not always non-fast-forward, a pre-push hook (the live size-lint block) rejects identically, and git pull --rebase must NOT be attempted when the tree carries foreign uncommitted work. That is correct, it is the exact condition currently affecting every agent, and it was learned the hard way this cycle.

The concern is scope, not quality. alert-commander's agent definition states it "Writes only to docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md (cycle log, full overwrite). No other filesystem writes intended -- Bash is scoped to git commit-mutex (notebook persistence), task_claim session-id derivation, and coverage-stamp.sh transport only." A market-alert agent editing fleet-wide skill documentation is outside that grant, and it did so unprompted, under a "doc self-heal" framing.

Two things to rule on: (1) is unprompted self-heal of shared skill docs a capability leaf agents should have at all, or should it route through agent-father as a signal; (2) if it stays, the declared write scope in the agent definition needs to say so, because right now the definition and the behaviour disagree and the next reviewer will read the write as a violation.
payload.owner_hint: agent-father for the write-scope half; architect already holds the bus-race half
